newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt sees 9.5 pct avge inflation in 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt sees 9.5 pct avge inflation in 1997.

text.p: Inflation was expected to average 9.5 percent in calendar 1997 but would decline in the latter part of the year, falling to 7.8 percent in the fourth quarter, Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said on Wednesday.
Answering a question in parliament, she said this was well in line with the Growth, Employment and Redistribution (GEAR) projection of an average 9.7 percent for the year.
"The latest economic forecasts show an inflation figure of around 9.5 percent for 1997," Marcus said.

"At present there are a number of counter-inflationary tendencies in the economy. These include the recent strengthening of the rand, fiscal prudence and a tight monetary policy. It is therefore anticipated that the forecast inflation rate in GEAR will be realised."
She added that the inflation projection of 9.5 percent for 1997 was consistent with the budget assumption of 8.5 percent for the fiscal year 1997/98 (April-March).
"This is because inflation is expected to drop to 7.8 percent in the fourth quarter of 1997 and reduce further in the first quarter of 1998."

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on Monday told investors attending a conference in Edinburgh that he expected inflation in the current fiscal year to run at an average 8.5 percent in the current fiscal year and to fall steadily thereafter.
